title: RA template import, version 1
description: A risk assessment template authored outside the tool and imported into the QHSE template manager (RS-26). Carries the hazard identification and its inherent severity, and nothing that is keyed to a tenant. Download the vocabulary manifest from the template manager first: it lists the effect categories with their axis level labels, plus the risk sources and exposure targets this tenant knows, so the file can be written with words that resolve. Every property is refused if misspelled, so a typo is reported rather than silently dropping the value.

$schema.description: Optional. Point an editor at this file for completion; the importer ignores it.

version.description: Format version. Absent, unrecognised and wrong-type are all refused the same way.

name.description: What the template is called. Templates carry no document number: a name plus a revision identifies one.

description.description: Optional. Stored as the template's scope: what it covers, and what it does not.

activities.description: The job in sequence. Array order is the only ordering the file carries; the importer derives sortOrder and displayNumber from it, so no identifiers appear anywhere in this format.

effectCategories.description: Which effect categories this activity is assessed against, by name ("Health") or standard ("ISO 45001") from the manifest. This decides how many scores each of its risks carries, so an activity with none is not merely unscored but unscorable.

risks.description: Risks are nested inside their activity. There is no parent reference, so a risk cannot dangle.

risk.description: One unwanted event. Barriers are deliberately absent from this format: a template's value is the hazard identification, and barriers are what the importing company decides to do about it.

event.description: The unwanted event. This is what the risk is.

riskSource.description: From the manifest's riskSources, by key or name. An unrecognised value is not an error: the importer asks about it once, with its usage count, and offers to map it, add it to the vocabulary, or leave it blank.

exposureTarget.description: What is harmed, from the manifest's exposureTargets. Reconciled the same way as riskSource.

minimumPpe.description: Protection this event demands. Per event, not per assessment: a chemical release and the noise beside it need different protection.

inherentScores.description: The hazard before any controls. Residual scores cannot be expressed in this format at all: R2 and R3 require a recorded barrier before an improvement is legitimate, barriers are not imported, and an imported residual would arrive unjustified.

effectCategory.description: By name or standard, from the manifest. A score whose category does not resolve is dropped and reported; its risk still imports.

consequence.description: Prefer the level label from that category's own ladder, which differs per category: on the reference tenant Health runs Not Dangerous or hazardous, Dangerous or hazardous, Critical, Very critical, Catastrophic, while Finance and Reputation run Negligible to Severe. A label is a statement about meaning; a number is a statement about position.

probability.description: As consequence. A level the destination axis does not have is refused, never clamped.
